knowledge:
- key_parameters: align_parents=logical, controls parent alignment during plotting and auto-hinting ;; normalize=logical, determines if input data frames should be checked and normalized ;; hints=list, contains custom plotting order (horder) and spouse matrix (spouse) ;; packed=logical, allows branches of the pedigree tree to overlap to save space ;; width=numeric, minimum width for a packed pedigree ;; align=logical, determines if children should be centered under parents ;; informative=character, criteria for identifying informative individuals (e.g., "AvAf") ;; max_bits=numeric, maximum size parameter used when shrinking pedigrees ;; ggplot_gen=logical, generates a ggplot object for interactive visualization
- alternatives: The documentation notes that "other software" is better suited for highly complex annotations or extremely large, heavily inbred pedigrees (such as in animal studies).
- when_to_use: Use when handling human family pedigree data, calculating kinship matrices (including sparse matrices for large multi-family studies), and generating automated, aligned pedigree plots.
- pitfalls: Do not use factors for subject identifiers (use character or numeric vectors instead) ;; Singletons (individuals with only one parent instead of two or none) can confuse the alignment setup ;; The diagonal elements of the kinship matrix are 0.5, not 1.0, which is a common point of genetic confusion ;; If errors are detected during normalization, the returned object contains an error column instead of a valid Pedigree.

workflows.name: pedigree_alignment_and_plotting
workflows.intent: Create a Pedigree object from family data, apply automatic or manual alignment hints, and plot the pedigree.
input: ped_df (data frame containing columns id, dadid, momid, sex, and optional status variables)
rel_df (optional data frame containing relationship pairs and codes for twins or spouses)
workflows.stages: 1. Construct the Pedigree object using Pedigree() ;; 2. Generate automatic alignment hints using auto_hint() ;; 3. Customize sibling ordering and spouse anchors using hints(), horder(), and spouse() ;; 4. Plot the pedigree using plot() or generate an interactive plot using ggplot_gen = TRUE and plotly
workflows.code:
id <- c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "J", "I", "H")
dadid <- c("0", "0", "0", "A", "C", "C", "A", "F", "F", "F")
momid <- c("0", "0", "0", "B", "B", "B", "E", "G", "G", "G")
sex <- c(1, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1, 2)
pedi <- Pedigree( id, dadid, momid, sex, na_strings = "0" )
plot(pedi, align_parents = FALSE, title = "1) Without reordering")
hints(pedi) <- auto_hint(pedi, align_parents = FALSE)
horder(hints(pedi))[c("H", "I", "J")] <- c(1, 2, 3)
spouse(hints(pedi)) <- data.frame(idl = "G", idr = "F", anchor = "left")
plot(pedi, align_parents = FALSE, title = "2) With ordering")

pedi <- Pedigree(sampleped)
p <- plot( pedi, ggplot_gen = TRUE, tips = c("affection", "momid", "dadid"), symbolsize = 1.5, cex = 0.8 )
plotly::layout( plotly::ggplotly(p$ggplot, tooltip = "text"), hoverlabel = list(bgcolor = "darkgrey") )

workflows.name: kinship_and_pedigree_subsetting
workflows.intent: Compute kinship matrices for family data, handle monozygotic twins, and subset or shrink pedigrees to informative individuals.
input: ped_df (data frame containing family pedigree data)
rel_df (optional data frame containing twin relationships)
workflows.stages: 1. Construct the Pedigree object using Pedigree() ;; 2. Compute the kinship matrix using kinship() ;; 3. Update family IDs and subset families using upd_famid() and bracket subsetting ;; 4. Shrink pedigrees to a target size using shrink() ;; 5. Filter for informative individuals using is_informative() and useful_inds()
workflows.code:
pedi <- Pedigree(sampleped[, -16])
kinship(pedi)[35:48, 35:48]

pedi <- Pedigree(sampleped)
mcols(pedi)$idth <- ifelse(as.numeric( stringr::str_split_i(id(ped(pedi)), "_", 2) ) < 200, "A", "B")
pedi <- upd_famid(pedi, mcols(pedi)$idth)
ped_a <- pedi[famid(ped(pedi)) == "A"]
lst1_s <- shrink(ped_a, max_bits = 10)
adopted(ped(ped_a)) <- FALSE
kinship(ped_a)[1:10, 1:10]
ped_a <- is_informative(ped_a, informative = "AvAf", col_aff = "affection")
ped_a <- useful_inds(ped_a)
as.data.frame(ped(ped_a))["useful"][1:10, ]
